newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PHILIP MORRIS UNIT TO RAISE CIGARETTE PRICES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PHILIP MORRIS UNIT TO RAISE CIGARETTE PRICES.

text.p: Tabak a.s., the Czech unit of U.S.-based Philip Morris Cos said on Wednesday that it was raising cigarette prices by up to one crown per pack, effective July 7.
"The main reason for this increase is the growth in production prices, mainly for tobacco which is purchased in U.S. dollars," a Tabak statement said.
The statement said the price of a package of king size cigarettes would rise by one crown, while packages of cigarettes of up to 70cm in length would rise by 0.5 crowns.

In May the Czech crown came under heavy pressure by speculators, which pushed the currency to record lows before the central bank was forced to freely float it. The crown has lost more than 18 percent of its value against the dollar this year.

Tabak produces many of the Czech Republic's most popular brands of cigarettes -- including Marlboros and Petras -- producing some 26 billion cigarettes in 1996. Tabak holds an estimated 80 market share in the Czech Republic.
